hints.title: Bipartite Array Sum Partition
hints.text: Checking all quadruplets takes O(N^4) operations. Partitioning the four lists into two pairs of lists reduces the dimensionality.

hints.title: Two Sum Map Lookup Invariant
hints.text: Precomputing all pairwise sums of nums1 and nums2 in a frequency map allows checking how many complement sums negative (c + d) exist from nums3 and nums4.

hints.title: Dual Quadratic Sum Accumulation Procedure
hints.text: Build a frequency mapping of sums for each pair (a, b) from nums1 and nums2. Initialize count to zero. Loop through all pairs (c, d) from nums3 and nums4. Add to count the frequency of negative (c + d) found in the mapping. Return count.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N^2) time and O(N^2) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Four nested loops across arrays of length 500 requires 500^4 = 6.25 * 10^10 operations, timing out completely.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Splitting four arrays into two pairs balances runtime to O(N^2) time and O(N^2) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize the meet-in-the-middle frequency table pattern and justify the optimal O(N^2) complexity.
